L3145: ## Conclusions
L3146: Assessment of 1G7 in the cotton rat model of RSV infection showed a reduction in RSV lung titers following challenge, which were approximately 6-fold and 4-fold greater than seen with palivizumab for RSV A and RSV B, respectively. These differences are lower than seen in cell culture, where 1G7 was approximately 180-fold and 150-fold more potent than palivizumab against RSV A2 and RSV B9320, respectively (Section 20.6).
L3147: ## 20.8.2. Assessment of Nirsevimab Impact on RSV Immunogenicity in Cotton Rat Model
L3148: Study report: ID8897-0032.
L3149: The cotton rat model of RSV infection was used to determine whether nirsevimab impacted the immune response to RSV infection.
L3150: ## Methodology
L3151: Cotton rats (n=12 animals per group) were injected intramuscularly at Day -1 with the test article 1G7 at 6 mg/kg, the nonrelevant control antibody R347 at 6 mg/kg or were untreated. Animals treated with mAbs were infected intranasally on Days 0 and 77 with 1 \times 10^6 pfu RSV A2, and the untreated control group was infected similarly only on Day 0. One other control group of 9 animals was treated with PBS and was only infected on Day 77, and another control group of 4 animals was treated with 6 mg/kg 1G7 and infected on Day 77. Animals were sacrificed 4 days after viral challenge, with 6 animals at Day 4 and Day 81 for each of the untreated, 1G7 and R347 groups and 3 for the PBS group at Day 4 and 6 at Day 81. The 4 animals in the 1G7 control group were sacrificed on Day 81.
L3152: RSV titers in lung and nasal turbinate samples were determined by plaque assay of homogenized tissues as described in Section 20.5.2. Human IgG was quantitated using ELISA as described in Section 20.8.1.
L3153: Neutralizing antibodies in serum samples were assessed using a cell-based fluorescent focus assay, using RSV expressing green fluorescent protein (GFP). Serum samples were heat inactivated at 56°C for 45 minutes and 3-fold serially diluted from a 1:8 starting dilution (final dilution 1:16) in 96-well plates. Palivizumab as a control was diluted similarly. Each dilution was mixed with RSV A2 GFP at 1,500 focus-forming units (FFU) per well and incubated for 2 hours at 37°C. HEp-2 cells at 5 \times 10^4 cells per well were added, and plates incubated for 20-22 hours at 37°C. Cells were then fixed with formalin and GFP positive cells counted using an ImageXpress Micro XLS plate reader (Molecular Devices), and the \log_2 of the IC_{50} value for each serum sample determined. The limit of detection for this assay was 4 \log_2.
L3154: ## Results
L3155: Figure 80 shows the RSV titers in lung and nasal turbinate tissue at 4 days postinfection. The viral titers in both lung and nasal turbinate tissues of the animals in the 1G7 group were below the limit of detection (16.7 pfu/g of tissue and 14.6 pfu/g of tissue, respectively). For the untreated group, an average viral titer of 1.66 \times 10^5 pfu/g of lung tissue was observed, similar to the mean viral titers measured in animals treated with the control mAb R347 (1.33 \times 10^5 pfu/g lung tissue).
L3156: The remaining animals were left until Day 68 to allow for complete clearance of serum mAb, at which point they were bled, and human IgG titers measured in serum. 1G7 serum concentrations were not detectable in both 1G7-treated groups, and the control R347 mAb was decreased to an average of 0.2 mg/mL (data not shown).

L3161: Animals were bled on Day 76 postchallenge and RSV neutralizing antibody titers determined (Figure 81). Neither group which was mock-infected on Day 0 showed detectable titers of anti-RSV neutralizing antibodies, whereas anti-RSV antibodies were detected for all groups infected on Day 0. Anti-RSV titers were not statistically significantly different between challenge groups, with mean antibody titers of 8.5 \times 10^3, 3.8 \times 10^3, and 12.8 \times 10^3 for the mock-treated, 1G7-treated, and R347-treated groups, respectively.

L3167: Cotton rats were challenged with RSV A2 on Day 77 and RSV titers measured in lung and nasal turbinates on Day 81 (Figure 82). High viral titers were seen in groups treated with PBS or 1G7 and were mock infected on Day 0 (lung: 2.33 \times 10^5 and 2.43 \times 10^5 pfu/g of tissue, respectively; nasal turbinates: 7.53 \times 10^4 and 1.15 \times 10^5 pfu/g of tissue, respectively). Animals which were untreated or treated with 1G7 or R347 and challenged with RSV on Day 0 did not have measurable titers of RSV at Day 81 following the second challenge (limit of detection [LOD] for lung and nasal turbinate tissue = 16.7 pfu/g and 14.6 pfu/g, respectively). Hence, these animals appeared to have developed an effective immune response to RSV which was protective against a second challenge.

L3172: ## Conclusions
L3173: In a cotton rat challenge study, animals treated prophylactically with 1G7 and challenged one day later with RSV, developed an immune response to RSV, as measured by the presence of serum neutralizing antibodies on Day 76, which was protective against subsequent challenge on Day 77. 1G7 is not modified with YTE substitutions in the Fc region, so would be expected to have been cleared by the time of the second challenge (although in rodents, YTE substitutions decrease antibody exposure; (Dall'Acqua et al. 2006)). Hence, in this model, 1G7 did not appear to significantly impact the development of an immune response to RSV, despite preventing the establishment of measurable titers of RSV in lung and nasal turbinates following the initial challenge. It is not clear whether these results can be extrapolated to humans, however.
L3174: Antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE) of infection, in terms of enhancement of RSV titers, was not observed in this study, or other experiments with the cotton rat model (Section 20.8.1), at sub-neutralizing doses down to 0.125 mg/kg for the RSV A2 challenge study and 0.03125 mg/kg for RSV B9320. While ADE of RSV infection has been demonstrated for mAbs in immune cell culture, no correlation between cell culture ADE and disease severity in infants has been demonstrated to date (van Erp et al. 2019).

L3384: ## Executive Summary
L3385: This submission is part of the Biologics License Application for nirsevimab, which is a respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) F protein inhibitor monoclonal antibody (mAb) indicated for the prevention of RSV lower respiratory tract disease in: neonates and infants entering or during their first RSV season and children up to 24 months of age who remain vulnerable to severe RSV disease through their second RSV season. Nirsevimab is a recombinant human IgG1k mAb that binds with high affinity to a highly conserved, discontinuous neutralizing epitope (AA 62 to 69 and AA 196 to 212) within antigenic site Ø (AA 62 to 96 and AA 195 to 227) on the pre-fusion confirmation of the RSV F protein. The primary Clinical Virology review of this application was performed by Dr. Michael Thomson, Ph.D. (see review BLA761328.000). This review was specifically performed for the assessment of next generation nucleotide sequencing (NGS) data submitted in support of the BLA.
L3386: A spot check independent review of the NGS data from a total of 43 subjects from Study 3 (D5290C00003; NCT02878330), MELODY (D5290C00004; NCT03979313), and MEDLEY (D5290C00005; NCT03959488) who met the primary case definition of medically attended (MA) RSV lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI), with or without hospitalization was performed by mapping fastq files from each subject to an RSV A or RSV F-gene reference sequence and comparing the substitutions and frequencies. The NGS sequencing results generated by DAV were largely in agreement with the results reported by the Applicant. No information associated with resistance was obtained from the independent review of NGS data in large part because of the prevention trial design precluding a treatment-emergent resistance analyses. This application is approvable from the Clinical Virology perspective based on the review of the primary Clinical Virology reviewer (see review BLA761328.000).
L3387: ## BACKGROUND
L3388: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), a member of the Pneumoviridae family (Rima et al., 2017), is a non-segmented, negative-sense, enveloped RNA virus and is classified into two subtypes, A and B, based on sequence homology of the RSV surface glycoprotein G (Wertz and Moudy, 2004). RSV entry into host cells and cell-to-cell spread is dependent on the fusion (F) protein, which mediates fusion of the viral and host cell membranes (Walsh et al., 1984, Walsh et al., 1989). The F protein is a highly conserved protein across RSV subtypes (Wertz and Moudy, 2004) and is produced as an inactive full-length precursor (AA 1-574) that is cleaved by host cell proteases into the biologically active, disulfide-linked F1 and F2 subunits, known as the extracellular region (F2: AA 24-109 and F1: AA 137-524) of the mature RSV F protein. The F protein is expressed on virions in a prefusion conformation. Juxtaposing of the virus and host cell membranes leads to the F protein-mediated fusion event and the accompanying irreversible refolding of F protein into a post-fusion conformation (Chang and Dutch, 2012). Six antigenic sites (Ø and I-V) have been identified in pre-fusion and/or post-fusion F proteins (Gilman et al., 2016) with target epitopes for prophylactic neutralizing mAbs (Broadbent et al., 2015).
L3389: Nirsevimab is a recombinant human IgG1k mAb that binds with high affinity to a highly conserved, discontinuous neutralizing epitope (AA: 62 to 69 and AA: 196 to 212) within antigenic site Ø (AA: 62 to 96 and AA: 195 to 227) on the pre-fusion confirmation of the RSV F protein. Nirsevimab has been engineered with a triple amino acid substitution (M252Y/S254T/T256E [YTE]) in the Fc region to prolong serum half-life of the mAb. For a comprehensive review of this application and all pertinent background information, please see the primary Clinical Virology review of this application, which was performed by Dr. Michael Thomson, Ph.D. (see review BLA761328.000).

L3409: ## **Overview of the Applicant's NGS Methodology**
L3410: The Applicant reported that the potential emergence of neutralization escape variants that may impact efficacy and effectiveness of nirsevimab was monitored throughout the development program with clinical (ID8897-cVAP-001; cVAP) and surveillance (ID8897-sVAP-002; sVAP) virology analysis plans to track the prevalence and emergence of F protein sequence variations among RSV isolates and evaluate the impact of these

L3412: ## VIROLOGY REVIEW
L3413: BLA#: 761328
L3414: DATE REVIEWED: 12/10/2022 to 3/23/2023
L3415: changes on cell culture susceptibility to neutralization. The sVAP (ID8897-svap-002) describes samples analyzed, sample collection (nasal samples) and workflow, performance characteristics of assays and methodologies, and analysis and reporting plans to support resistance monitoring of surveillance RSV isolates. The data for the independent review of NGS samples were derived via the cVAP (ID8897-cVAP-001).
L3416: The cVAP (ID8897-cVAP-001) for all pivotal studies contributing to the clinical efficacy of nirsevimab was previously described in Report ID8897-cVAP-001. Respiratory samples were obtained from all subjects found to have an LRTI and all subjects who required hospitalization for a respiratory infection (even without diagnosis of an LRTI). The resistance analysis population included any subject in any treatment group and any reporting period with a respiratory sample that tested positive for RSV by central laboratory RT-PCR with an evaluable NGS sequence.
L3417: All RT-PCR confirmed RSV isolates were subtyped and evaluated by genotypic and phenotypic resistance analysis methodologies as previously described (see Report ID8897-cVAP-001). Genotypic analyses were performed using a validated NGS method to detect major (\ge 25\% frequency within each sample) and minor (\ge 4\% and \ge 5\% LLOQ frequency within each sample of RSV A and B, respectively) viral variants. For completeness, data up to the limit of detection (\ge 2\% frequency) are additionally provided. The data were divided into major (substitutions that were observed in \ge 25\% of the viral sequences from each sample) and minor variants (substitutions that were observed in \ge 4\% for RSV A and \ge 5\% RSV B). Subjects were counted once for each category within a reporting period, with the exception of subjects who had different RSV subtype infections within a reporting period. For subjects with multiple RSV positive samples within a reporting period, the first specimen from each illness episode is analyzed in summary data. Listings are provided for subjects with more than one respiratory specimen.
L3418: The NGS analyses were performed by [REDACTED] (b) (4) using Illumina MiSeq technology generating 250 bp paired-end reads. FASTQ files were analyzed in CLC Genomics Workbench to determine frequency of minor variants. RSV F nucleotide reads were mapped to Netherlands RSV A/13-5275 or Netherlands RSV B/13-1273 reference sequences, followed by variant calling and amino acid annotation. Results were exported from CLC Genomics Workbench as tab-delimited text files.
L3419: Variant frequency tables were generated to depict amino acid changes identified in the full-length RSV F protein (AA 1 to 574), including the nirsevimab (AA 62 to 69 and AA 196 to 212) and palivizumab (AA 262 to 275) binding sites, that differ from 2013 Netherlands reference strains (Netherlands RSV A/13-5275 or Netherlands RSV B/13-1273). RSV F protein sequence variations detected among clinical isolates were categorized as polymorphic if they were detected among surveillance RSV isolates since 2015 and nonpolymorphic if they had not been detected. Prevalence of all RSV F protein sequence variations were reported relative to consensus sequences of recent circulating RSV A and RSV B strains since February 2015.
L3420: ## Overview of DAV NGS Analysis Methodology
L3421: The CLC Genomics Workbench (V22.0, Qiagen Ca. USA) was used to perform the independent assessment of the NGS data for this BLA. The CLC Genomics Workbench tool contains specific tools that allow the reviewer to batch rename files to meet nomenclature rules for the analysis pipeline, trim reads, map reads to a reference sequence, determine low-frequency variant calls, and export variant call files (VCF) in Excel.
L3422: **The CLC Genomics Workbench.** Briefly, the workflow in CLC Genomics workbench was as follows: trimmed reads were mapped to the RSV A (2013 Netherlands RSV A/13-005275; KX858757.1) or RSV B (Netherlands RSV B/13-001273; KX858756.1) F gene reference sequence as appropriate and variants in the RSV F gene were called at the amino acid level using the low frequency variant caller. The parameters used in CLC Genomics were the following:
L3423: - Mapping using CLC read mapping alignerMatch score: 1
- Mismatch cost: 2
- Insertion cost: 3
- Deletion cost: 3
- Length fraction of read required for mapping: 0.5

L3429: Each step of the NGS analysis process is briefly described below.
L3430: - **Processing fastq files.** Data were submitted to the FDA on a portable hard drive, which included fastq files for each subject's samples that were sequenced using paired end chemistry and the Illumina MiSeq sequencing platform. The nucleotide sequences were uploaded via the CLC Genomics interface and renamed to conform with DAV nomenclature preferences.
- **Preparing sequence reads and reference sequences prior to mapping.** The fastq files were imported into CLC Genomics and reads were mapped to the RSV A (2013 Netherlands RSV A/13-005275; KX858757.1) or RSV B (Netherlands RSV B/13-001273; KX858756.1) F gene reference sequence as appropriate. The F gene was annotated as a coding sequence to establish the correct amino acid number for the gene. The individual reads from each fastq file were subjected to trimming using the default parameters for CLC Genomics Workbench (when used).
- **Mapping reads to the appropriate reference sequence.** The reads from each fastq file were aligned to the appropriate reference sequence to generate a mapping for each sample. The mapping contained the target of interest (F gene sequences) and was used to identify variants that differed from the reference sequence. In general, the mappings were assessed to determine the depth of coverage at each nucleotide position and to evaluate read directionality (ratio of forward to reverse reads) to identify regions of bias.
- **Generating frequency tables of amino acid substitutions.** From the read mappings, variants were identified and variant files were generated using the Low Frequency Variant Detector in CLC Genomics workbench. The variant call files were exported to Excel and converted into amino acid frequency tables. Here is a description of frequency table generation:**Low Frequency Variant Detection (LFVD)** – according to the CLC Genomics Workbench Manual: “a statistical test is performed at each site to determine if the nucleotides observed in the reads at that site could be due simply to sequencing errors, or if they are significantly better explained by there being one (or more) alleles than the reference present in the sample at some unknown frequency. If the latter is the case, a variant corresponding to the significant allele will be called, with estimated frequency”.
- **Frequency tables** – Tables were generated using from the CLC genomics VCF exported in Excel. Information for each position of each gene and each subject for which variation from the reference occurs was exported. The frequency table contains the following columns: unique subject identifier (USUBJID), treatment regimen (ARM), visit (VISIT), the amino acid position within the gene of interest (AAPOS), total coverage at the nucleotide position (TCOV), the amino acid found in the reference sequence (AAREF), the amino acid substitution (AASUB), the coverage at the nucleotide level for the variant (VCOV), and the frequency by which the variant was detected (AAFREQ). Frequency tables are generated by:The variant tables were combined by subtype (RSV A or RSV B)

L3462: Overall, the results obtained in the independent analysis were consistent with the results reported by the Applicant with the following exceptions:
L3463: - E2G (n=1) was detected by DAV but not the Applicant at 99% frequency in subject (b) (6) who was infected with RSV B. This substitution was detected in one subject who received NIR; however, the substitution is outside of the NIR epitope and has not been associated with resistance. This was likely
L3464: ## DIVISION OF ANTIVIRAL PRODUCTS (HFD-530)
L3465: ## VIROLOGY REVIEW
L3466: BLA#: 761328
L3467: DATE REVIEWED: 12/10/2022 to 3/23/2023
L3468: in the primer region and was trimmed by the Applicant during NGS analysis,
L3469: - The substitution Y306H was detected by DAV but not reported by the Applicant at a frequency range of 6-11% in all 20 subjects who had RSV B and had sequence data available, including subjects who received PBO (n=5), NIR (n=13) or PAL (n=2). Of note, the positioning of this substitution within the sequence reads that contained this substitution was analyzed to determine if it was associated with anomalies characterized in the known error profile for Illumina MiSeq platform. This substitution resulted from a TAT to CAT codon mutation, occurred in various portions of the read at a high-quality score, and does not appear to be associated with a homopolymer sequence. The substitution cannot be ruled out based on sequence error, and it is unknown why it is detected by DAV but not the Applicant. However, given that it occurred in all treatment groups in subjects with RSV B and the amino acid position does not fall within the NIR epitope, it is unlikely to be associated with NIR treatment or resistance.
- In clinical trial MELODY (D5290C00004; NCT03979313) there was a frequency and coverage discrepancy between DAV and the Applicant pertaining to substitutions I384V (subject (b) (6) from the NIR treatment group), N515H (subjects (b) (6) from the NIR treatment group and (b) (6) from the PBO treatment group), and A540S (subjects (b) (6) from the NIR treatment group and (b) (6) from the PBO treatment group). In general, this discrepancy appears to be related to differences in coverage as the Applicant reported coverages of 10-fold greater depth at these positions compared to the data generated by DAV. The exact reason for the differences in coverage are not clear; however, given that these substitutions are outside of the NIR epitope at positions that are not associated with resistance, occurred in subjects from the NIR and PBO treatment groups, and were detected by both DAV and the Applicant (albeit at different frequencies) it is unlikely that these substitutions are associated with NIR treatment or resistance.
L3470: **Conclusion:** The NGS sequencing results generated by DAV were largely in agreement with the results reported by the Applicant. No information associated with resistance was obtained from the independent review of NGS data in large part because the sequence information provided was not supportive of a treatment-emergent resistance analyses. This application is approvable from the Clinical Virology perspective based on the review of the primary Clinical Virology reviewer (see review BLA761328.000).
L3471: ## CONCLUSIONS
L3472: - This submission is part of the Biologics License Application for nirsevimab, which is a RSV F protein inhibitor mAb indicated for the prevention of RSV lower respiratory tract disease in: neonates and infants entering or during their first RSV season and children up to 24 months of age who remain vulnerable to severe RSV disease through their second RSV season.
- Nirsevimab is a recombinant human IgG1k mAb that binds with high affinity to a highly conserved, discontinuous neutralizing epitope (AA 62 to 69 and AA 196 to 212) within antigenic site Ø (AA 62 to 96 and AA 195 to 227) on the pre-fusion confirmation of the RSV F protein.
- The primary Clinical Virology review of this application was performed by Dr. Michael Thomson, Ph.D. (see review BLA761328.000).
- This review was specifically performed for the assessment of NGS data submitted in support of the BLA.
- The nomenclature for the NGS files was not optimal in allowing for the substantial review of the NGS data and would not be acceptable for review of large treatment-emergent resistance assessments under normal circumstances. However, given that the sequence data were primarily of a surveillance nature and were comprised of limited temporal samples, a spot check independent review of the NGS data from 43 subjects from 3 clinical trials was performed.
- The NGS sequencing results generated by DAV were largely in agreement with the results reported by

L3534: Figure 7 is a timeline diagram illustrating the trial design for Trial 04, showing the study phases from Day 1 to Day 511. The timeline is divided into two parallel arms: Nirsevimab single IM dose (top, yellow bar) and Placebo single IM dose (saline) (bottom, blue bar).
The process starts with Informed consent, followed by Screening. Randomization occurs at a 2:1 ratio, assigning subjects to either the Nirsevimab or Placebo arm.
The Nirsevimab arm includes the Dosing phase (Day 1 to Day 150) and the Efficacy endpoint phase (Day 151 to Day 361). The Placebo arm includes the Dosing phase (Day 1 to Day 150) and the Safety follow-up phase (Day 151 to Day 361). Both arms continue through Day 511.

Three treatments are compared: Nirsevimab (blue circles), Palivizumab (green triangles), and R347 (black triangles). Nirsevimab and Palivizumab show increasing phagocytic scores with concentration, peaking around 10 \mug/mL. R347 shows minimal activity.
B.
Bar chart showing Area Under the Curve (AUC) for Phagocytic Score. Nirsevimab AUC is approximately 3500. Palivizumab AUC is approximately 5000. R347 AUC is near 0. No significant difference (ns) is noted between Nirsevimab and Palivizumab, and no significant difference (ns) is noted between Palivizumab and R347.
L3604: Figure 73 displays the results of the Antibody-Dependent Complement Deposition (ADCD) assay. Panel A is a dose-response curve showing Complement Deposition (gMFI) versus Concentration (\mug/mL) on a logarithmic scale. Nirsevimab and Palivizumab show high complement deposition, peaking around 1 \mug/mL. R347 shows minimal deposition. Panel B is a bar chart showing the Area Under the Curve (AUC) for complement deposition. Nirsevimab and Palivizumab have significantly higher AUC values compared to R347, with an asterisk indicating statistical significance (p < 0.05).
L3605: Figure 74 displays the ADNKA-CD107a activity of Nirsevimab, Palivizumab, and R347 across two donors (A and B) and the Area Under the Curve (AUC) analysis (C).
A. Donor A: A dose-response curve showing the percentage of CD107a+ NK cells (Y-axis, 0 to 60%) versus concentration (X-axis, log scale, 0.001 to 100 \mug/mL). Nirsevimab (blue circles) and Palivizumab (green triangles) show increasing activity with concentration, reaching approximately 20-25% CD107a+ NK cells at 10 \mug/mL. R347 (black triangles) shows minimal activity, remaining below 5%.
B. Donor B: A dose-response curve showing the percentage of CD107a+ NK cells (Y-axis, 0 to 60%) versus concentration (X-axis, log scale, 0.001 to 100 \mug/mL). Nirsevimab (blue circles) and Palivizumab (green triangles) show increasing activity with concentration, reaching approximately 40-45% CD107a+ NK cells at 10 \mug/mL. R347 (black triangles) shows minimal activity, remaining below 5%.
C. AUC Analysis: A bar chart comparing the Area Under the Curve (AUC) values for Nirsevimab (blue bar, approximately 280), Palivizumab (green bar, approximately 290), and R347 (black bar, approximately 50). The difference between Nirsevimab and Palivizumab is labeled as 'ns' (not significant).
L3606: Figure 75 displays the ADCC activity of Nirsevimab, Palivizumab, and R347 across five donors (A-E) and a summary bar chart (F).
Plots A-E show % Specific Lysis versus Concentration (\mug/mL) on a logarithmic scale (0.001 to 100). The Y-axis ranges from 0 to 80% Specific Lysis.
Donor A: Nirsevimab and Palivizumab show high activity, reaching approximately 65% lysis at 10 \mug/mL. R347 shows negligible activity.
Donor B: Nirsevimab and Palivizumab show moderate activity, reaching approximately 25% lysis at 10 \mug/mL. R347 shows negligible activity.
Donor C: Nirsevimab and Palivizumab show moderate activity, reaching approximately 20% lysis at 10 \mug/mL. R347 shows negligible activity.
Donor D: Nirsevimab and Palivizumab show low activity, reaching approximately 10% lysis at 10 \mug/mL. R347 shows negligible activity.
Donor E: Nirsevimab and Palivizumab show moderate activity, reaching approximately 50% lysis at 10 \mug/mL. R347 shows negligible activity.
Plot F: Area Under the Curve (AUC) analysis comparing Nirsevimab, Palivizumab, and R347. Nirsevimab AUC is approximately 700, Palivizumab AUC is approximately 800, and R347 AUC is approximately 100. The difference between Nirsevimab and Palivizumab is marked as 'ns' (not significant).
L3607: Figure 76 displays two graphs showing the antiviral activity of 1G7, Palivizumab, 3649 (negative control), cells and virus, and cells alone against RSV A2 (left) and RSV B9320 (right). The Y-axis represents absorbance at 450 nm (A_{450nm}), and the X-axis represents MAb concentration in ng/mL (log scale).
RSV A2 Graph: 1G7 (green circles) shows potent neutralization, with A_{450nm} dropping significantly below 0.5 at 1 ng/mL. Palivizumab (purple crosses) also shows strong neutralization, dropping below 0.5 at 10 ng/mL. 3649 (black crosses) and cells alone (black squares) show minimal effect.
RSV B9320 Graph: 1G7 (green circles) shows potent neutralization, with A_{450nm} dropping significantly below 0.5 at 1 ng/mL. Palivizumab (purple crosses) also shows strong neutralization, dropping below 0.5 at 100 ng/mL. 3649 (black crosses) and cells alone (black squares) show minimal effect.
L3608: Figure 77 displays two graphs showing the antiviral activity of 1G7 and MEDI8897 (nirsevimab) against RSV A2 (left) and RSV B9320 (right). The Y-axis represents absorbance at 450 nm (A_{450nm}), and the X-axis represents MAb concentration in ng/mL (log scale).
Activity against RSV A2: Both 1G7 (green circles) and MEDI8897 (blue triangles) show potent neutralization, with A_{450nm} dropping significantly below 0.5 at 1 ng/mL.
Activity Against RSV B9320: Both 1G7 (green circles) and MEDI8897 (blue triangles) show potent neutralization, with A_{450nm} dropping significantly below 0.5 at 1 ng/mL.
L3609: Figure 78: Distribution of EC50 Values for RSV A and RSV B Clinical Isolates. The plot shows EC50 Values (ng/mL) on a logarithmic scale (0.1 to 100) versus RSV A isolates (n=70) and RSV B isolates (n=49). The RSV A isolates (red dots) show a median EC50 value around 3.2 ng/mL. The RSV B isolates (blue dots) show a median EC50 value around 2.9 ng/mL. Both distributions are centered around 1 ng/mL, with medians and interquartile ranges indicated by horizontal lines.
L3610: Figure 79 displays two graphs showing the antiviral activity of 1G7 and Palivizumab in the Cotton Rat Model of RSV Infection. The left graph is for RSV A2, and the right graph is for RSV 9320. Both graphs plot Lung Titer (log base 10 pfu/g) on the Y-axis against IgG concentration (µg/mL) on the X-axis (log scale). Data points represent measurements from individual animals. The dashed line indicates the Limit of Detection (LOD). In both graphs, 1G7 (green squares) shows a dose-dependent reduction in lung titer, reaching the LOD at higher concentrations. Palivizumab (red circles) also shows a dose-dependent reduction, but requires higher concentrations than 1G7 to achieve similar reductions. The 'No MAb' group (black triangles) shows high lung titers.
L3611: Figure 80 shows two scatter plots comparing PFU/g Lung Tissue (left) and PFU/g NT Tissue (right) four days post-RSV challenge (Day 4) across four groups: PBS, Mock, 1G7, and R347. The y-axis is logarithmic (Log10). A dashed line indicates the LOD (Limit of Detection). For Lung Tissue, Mock, 1G7, and R347 groups show significantly higher titers than PBS (***p<0.0001). For NT Tissue, Mock and 1G7 groups show significantly higher titers than PBS (*p<0.05). R347 is not significantly different from PBS. RSV IN immunization at Day 0 is indicated below the x-axis.
L3612: Figure 81 is a scatter plot showing Neutralizing antibody titers (Log2) versus wt RSV A2 IN immunization at day 0. The x-axis groups are PBS, -, 1G7, R347, and 1G7. The y-axis ranges from 0 to 16. A dashed line indicates the limit of detection (LOD). The PBS group shows low titers (around 4). The -, 1G7, R347, and 1G7 groups show significantly higher titers (around 12-14). The difference between the -, 1G7, R347, and 1G7 groups is marked as NS (Not Significant).
L3613: Figure 82 displays two scatter plots showing RSV titers (PFU/g Tissue, Log10 scale) in lung and nasal turbinates (NT) four days postintranasal challenge with RSV (Day 81). The x-axis groups are PBS, Mock, 1G7, R347, and 1G7. The y-axis is logarithmic, ranging from 10^0 to 10^5. The horizontal dashed line indicates the Limit of Detection (LOD). The left plot shows Lung Tissue titers. The right plot shows NT Tissue titers. Statistical significance is indicated by asterisks above the groups: *** for PBS vs Mock, *** for PBS vs 1G7, ** for Mock vs 1G7, and *** for Mock vs R347. The legend indicates LOD (Limit of Detection).
